CME Trade Plans and Risk Management

guides.title: Why enter, hold, exit or wait: the decision framework
guides.concept: An entry is a decision made before outcomes are known; holding requires a still-valid thesis and acceptable current risk, while exits and no-trade choices come from previously identified conditions.
guides.watchFor: Record timeframe, session, candidate quality, catalyst if relevant, observed structure, level, trigger, volume scope, available spread, stop thesis and intended duration before judging a plan.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry is discussable only after the chosen trigger is visible at the decision timestamp and risk and order feasibility have been independently assessed.
guides.holdEvidence: An open example position remains compatible with the original plan only while the setup premise and confirmation hold, current exposure is known, and no planned exit or time limit is reached.
guides.exitEvidence: An invalidated level, breached risk budget, elapsed time stop, verified adverse news, lost structure or reached planned exit rule calls for exit review; actual execution may differ from the model.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when the trigger has not occurred or the candle is provisional. NO TRADE when data, liquidity, acceptable risk or the required conditions are missing.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: At 10:07 a bar is still forming at a resistance zone. The setup is visible but a close-based trigger has not occurred; classify as WAIT, not an already-confirmed entry.
guides.procedure: At a declared replay pause point, first check the setup and source constraints. Record timeframe, session, candidate quality, catalyst if relevant, observed structure, level, trigger, volume scope, available spread, stop thesis and intended duration before judging a plan.
guides.limit: No stated condition proves a profitable trading edge, a future candle, a fill price, or suitability for an individual member. Conditions are instructional examples, not trading instructions.
guides.invalidation: The declared price/time condition fails, risk becomes unmanageable, or required source or execution evidence is missing. This must be distinguished from a guaranteed stop fill.
guides.commonError: Treating a familiar pattern name or past outcome as sufficient justification for a new entry, then rewriting the original hold or exit rule after seeing price.
guides.selfCheck: For this setup, explain the observed entry trigger, one evidence-based hold condition, one invalidation/exit event, and one WAIT or NO TRADE reason before a future candle is shown.
guides.reviewExplanation: A correct ungraded explanation uses the known timestamp, observable condition, risk boundary and the possibility of no trade; holding is conditional and exit execution is not guaranteed.

guides.title: Breakout entry hold exit decision and confirmation
guides.concept: A breakout attempts to leave a previously observed range; acceptance and volume context can support a hypothesis but never establish future continuation.
guides.watchFor: First establish the ceiling and floor from completed bars, timeframe, relative volume with matched interval, and whether the break is a provisional tick or completed trigger.
guides.entryEvidence: Consider an illustrative entry only after the predefined confirmation criterion is observed and a plausible invalidation and executable spread are recorded.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is supported only while the break remains accepted under the declared rule, follow-through structure develops, and a planned risk or time limit is not breached.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a return under the breakout reference, deteriorating structure, the planned target/time condition or unmanageable spread; never rewrite the original threshold afterward.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for unconfirmed breakouts; NO TRADE if the expansion has poor liquidity, lacks required participation or the distance to invalidation makes modeled risk unacceptable.

guides.title: Breakout retest and support-resistance role reversal
guides.concept: A retest examines whether a previously broken ceiling behaves as a support area; a touch alone is not a completed acceptance or a fill guarantee.
guides.watchFor: Mark the original level before the breakout, wait for the subsequent test to become observable, and assess the hold/reclaim behavior against a predefined bar/time rule.
guides.entryEvidence: An example retest entry requires the documented test-and-response trigger rather than a hypothetical perfect low, with an invalidation point and feasible modeled costs.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold reasoning depends on the retested level and subsequent higher-low or acceptance structure remaining intact while the risk plan remains valid.
guides.exitEvidence: A sustained failure back into the old range, violated retest low, or changed risk condition challenges the thesis and motivates exit evaluation.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if the first retest candle is unfinished; NO TRADE if the level cannot be located objectively or repeated whipsaws remove decision quality.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A completed breakout above $11.60 is followed by a return to $11.62; nothing yet shows whether buyers can support the level. Touch alone does not authorize a hindsight entry.

guides.title: Failed breakout rejection and trapped-position hypothesis
guides.concept: A failed breakout is an attempted break that later loses its predeclared acceptance condition; the later rejection must not be smuggled into the earlier decision.
guides.watchFor: Record prior range edge, first breakout timestamp, required hold rule, later return inside and whether the supposed failure is based on completed observations.
guides.entryEvidence: A hypothetical failure setup becomes analyzable only after the chosen inside-range rejection condition is actually observed, alongside direction-specific liquidity and risk checks.
guides.holdEvidence: A short-side or mean-reverting hypothesis remains intact only while price stays rejected below the old ceiling under the chosen rule; short borrow and halt risk are separate.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a regained ceiling, false-failure diagnosis, fulfilled time or target condition, or unmanageable short/borrow exposure.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when rejection is only an active candle; NO TRADE without an objectively identified range, liquid quotes and short-side access where needed.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: $16.40 was resistance at 09:50, then price closed $16.52; the first completed close back below $16.40 occurs at 10:05. Earlier inference cannot use that event.

guides.title: Uptrend pullback entry hold exit and EMA context
guides.concept: A pullback is a countertrend retracement within a larger price structure, which might be ordinary consolidation or the beginning of a reversal.
guides.watchFor: Establish higher timeframe HH/HL structure, the chosen moving-average settings, prior swing support, retracement depth, volume interpretation and the exact resumption rule.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative entry case requires an observed resumption signal after the retracement, not merely an EMA touch, with a preplanned structure-based invalidation.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold reasoning requires the accepted support/higher-low thesis to remain true and price action to follow the selected trend-management rule; a green candle alone is insufficient.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a confirmed structure break, invalidation, failed bounce, risk threshold or predetermined time/target rule.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when the pullback is still descending without resumption; NO TRADE if trend and trigger timeframes conflict or a stop cannot be feasibly modeled.

guides.title: VWAP reclaim entry hold exit and session acceptance
guides.concept: VWAP is a volume-weighted session or anchor reference; a reclaim pattern is defined by an observed transition across that reference plus a specified acceptance rule.
guides.watchFor: Verify the anchor, data feed, extended-hours inclusion, bar calculation and whether price has reclaimed and held under the planned decision timeframe.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry requires a completed acceptance or retest trigger as predefined, plus separate liquidity and risk checks; a single active tick above VWAP is not enough.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires the documented above-VWAP acceptance and supporting structure to remain observable, with price not violating the defined invalidation or duration.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows failure of the reclaim condition, renewed rejection below VWAP, a structure break or the preplanned time/target condition.
guides.noTrade: WAIT through mixed provisional crosses. NO TRADE in repeated chop or when the VWAP anchors/feed cannot be reconciled.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: Regular-session VWAP is $14.22 at 10:10; a one-minute live candle crosses to $14.25 but closes below at $14.19. A close-based reclaim was not confirmed.

guides.title: VWAP rejection and downside-continuation hypothesis
guides.concept: A VWAP rejection pattern describes a test of a properly anchored VWAP that fails to maintain a selected acceptance condition; it is not evidence that price must fall.
guides.watchFor: Establish current session VWAP, higher-timeframe structure, low/high references and the timestamp of the attempted test and completed rejection.
guides.entryEvidence: An educational bearish-entry hypothesis requires the predeclared rejection condition and a feasible short-side plan; a red candle at VWAP is not sufficient.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is conditional on price staying rejected under the selected rule and the downside structure and risk assumptions remaining valid.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows confirmed VWAP acceptance above the reference, a new higher-high structure, borrow disruption, risk limit or time exit.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for an incomplete rejection bar. NO TRADE with unreliable anchor, heavy choppiness, SSR/borrow uncertainties or unmanageable spread.

guides.title: Opening range breakout and first-session context
guides.concept: An opening range is a predefined early-session high/low window; its boundaries are only final after the chosen opening interval closes.
guides.watchFor: Specify clock timezone, 5/15/30 minute range length, regular session versus premarket, opening auction prints, accumulated volume and confirmation rules.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry requires the complete range and a later observed break that satisfies the declared trigger, with spread and volatility risk assessed.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires sustained acceptance outside that known range and the chosen continuation structure, while controlling rapid opening volatility.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a completed return inside the opening range, an invalidated pivot, risk violation or time-based plan expiration.
guides.noTrade: WAIT until the range completes. NO TRADE if premarket data are misclassified, spreads are abnormal, trading pauses intervene or there is no qualifying break.

guides.title: Gap continuation entry hold exit after catalyst verification

guides.watchFor: Record prior close, corporate-action adjustments, premarket session, official issuer filing/news timestamp, first regular-session structure and executable spreads.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative entry can be discussed only after a predefined regular-session continuation condition appears, with the gap-risk model and halt contingency addressed.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires the chosen morning structure and continuation condition to persist, rather than assuming gap size itself guarantees momentum.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows rejection into the gap, broken opening structure, loss of catalyst support or the predefined risk/time condition.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if the opening interval is incomplete. NO TRADE if a reverse split explains the apparent gap, the catalyst cannot be verified or execution is too wide.

guides.title: Gap fade and failed opening acceptance
guides.concept: A gap fade is a hypothesis that an opening repricing may retrace; fading a strong trend before failure evidence is not a confirmed reversal.
guides.watchFor: Document the gap from like-for-like adjusted prices, the opening high/low, premarket liquidity and a completed failure of the chosen continuation rule.
guides.entryEvidence: An example fade entry requires a visible rejection or failed-hold trigger at the declared level, not simply a large gap magnitude.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold can be considered while the fade thesis, lower-high/failed-reclaim structure and direction-specific risks remain intact.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a successful reclaim by price, trend resumption, reached target/time exit or an unacceptable squeeze risk.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for an actually observed failure. NO TRADE when gap news remains powerful, borrow is unavailable or a supposed fill is purely hypothetical.

guides.title: Range support resistance entry hold exit decision
guides.concept: A range trades between previously documented upper and lower boundaries, but either boundary can break and volatility may compress or expand.
guides.watchFor: Use completed reactions to define range zones, distance between boundaries, volume behavior and the specific reversal/hold requirement at the targeted boundary.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry is considered only after the selected boundary response is visible, with feasible reward-to-risk distance and planned invalidation beyond the zone.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is supported while the position remains inside the range under its prescribed mean-reversion thesis and price has not decisively violated the relevant boundary.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows reaching the opposing zone, failed response, confirmed breakout against the position, or a time/risk condition.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for evidence at the edge. NO TRADE in the middle of the box if the planned reward is too small after spreads and costs.

guides.title: Higher highs higher lows trend continuation and hold management
guides.concept: A continuation hypothesis uses already observed swing structure; holding does not mean ignoring changing risk or promising the next higher high.
guides.watchFor: Record HH/HL or LH/LL on a specified timeframe, completed swing confirmation, relative volume and whether a retracement violates a meaningful structural level.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative trend entry needs the chosen continuation or resumption event and a logical invalidation, not simply price moving up or down.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold remains a conditional choice when the original trend structure persists, planned time and risk constraints remain intact, and a newer stop approach is consistent with the plan.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows an observed structural change, broken key swing, momentum failure defined beforehand, completed time stop or target.

guides.title: Reversal entry hold exit after failed prior trend
guides.concept: A reversal requires evidence that the old trend lost its prior structure and a new structure is developing; a single opposite-color candle does not prove a trend turn.
guides.watchFor: Identify the old sequence, support/resistance break, follow-through or higher-low/lower-high sequence and compare volume in matched windows.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative reversal entry needs the predeclared structural confirmation and a risk level that makes the hypothesis falsifiable.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is conditionally supported only while the new structure progresses and the old trend's key level stays invalidated under the rule.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows a return to the previous trend structure, loss of the new swing level, or reaching planned risk/time limits.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for a confirmed countertrend pivot. NO TRADE if the evidence is just one wick, an unfinished bar or a news-driven halt.

guides.title: Support bounce, resistance rejection and level quality
guides.concept: An observed support or resistance reaction describes one interaction with a price zone, not evidence that the zone will hold forever.
guides.watchFor: Compare repeated completed interactions, volume scope, timeframe, width of the level zone and nearby opposite levels before defining a reaction rule.
guides.entryEvidence: An example level-based entry needs a confirmed reaction under the declared timeframe and a falsifiable stop/invalidation that accounts for normal price noise.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is a hypothesis while the chosen zone continues to contain the movement and the position's reward-to-risk remains acceptable.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows an established level break, confirmed failed retest, changed liquidity or risk threshold.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if a provisional candle is only touching the zone. NO TRADE if the level is too ambiguous or the opposing zone is too close after fees.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A level near $32.00 has three prior reactions. A new candle trades $31.99 before closing; the learner must apply the preset zone rule, not a hindsight single-cent threshold.
guides.procedure: At a declared replay pause point, first check the setup and source constraints. Compare repeated completed interactions, volume scope, timeframe, width of the level zone and nearby opposite levels before defining a reaction rule.
guides.limit: No stated condition proves a profitable trading edge, a future candle, a fill price, or suitability for an individual member. Conditions are instructional examples, not trading instructions.
guides.invalidation: The declared price/time condition fails, risk becomes unmanageable, or required source or execution evidence is missing. This must be distinguished from a guaranteed stop fill.
guides.commonError: Treating a familiar pattern name or past outcome as sufficient justification for a new entry, then rewriting the original hold or exit rule after seeing price.
guides.selfCheck: For this setup, explain the observed entry trigger, one evidence-based hold condition, one invalidation/exit event, and one WAIT or NO TRADE reason before a future candle is shown.
guides.reviewExplanation: A correct ungraded explanation uses the known timestamp, observable condition, risk boundary and the possibility of no trade; holding is conditional and exit execution is not guaranteed.

guides.title: Mean reversion to VWAP versus strong-trend continuation
guides.concept: Mean reversion hypothesizes movement toward a documented reference, but price can remain extended far longer than expected during strong directional sessions.
guides.watchFor: Define the mean/anchor, current excursion, distance in ATR or percent, opposing trend evidence, and the actual reversion trigger before forming a plan.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative reversion entry requires a demonstrated slowing/rejection or structural turn, not the mere distance from VWAP or an overbought oscillator.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is conditional on sustained reversion evidence and the preplanned destination and risk rules; a trend acceleration challenges the thesis.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows achieved reference/target, renewed extension against the thesis, time expiration, invalidation or execution-cost deterioration.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for confirmation and NO TRADE when the dominant trend is accelerating, market is halted or the model assumes guaranteed return to the mean.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: Price is 4% above VWAP at 11:00, but the first post-open trend keeps making confirmed higher lows. Distance from VWAP alone proves no reversal.

guides.title: Breakdown and short-side hold exit risk decision
guides.concept: A breakdown tests whether support has failed, but short-side execution adds borrow, recall, price-test restrictions, squeeze and halt risks absent from a simple long mirror image.
guides.watchFor: Record completed support zone and breakdown condition, matched volume, confirmed locate/borrow, live spread, reference session and stop/contingency.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative short entry can be discussed only with a confirmed bearish trigger and real permission/risk conditions, never solely because a candle is red.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold depends on continued acceptance below support, a still-valid downside thesis and monitored borrow, margin and exposure constraints.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows reclaimed support, squeeze/borrow/market disruption, violated planned risk or predefined target/time.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for completed confirmation. NO TRADE when short availability, SSR, quote reliability or downside liquidity cannot be verified.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: $8.20 is the observed range floor. A short thesis awaits a completed break; the tape shows only a transient $8.17 print, and broker locate status is unknown.

guides.title: News catalyst continuation versus sell-the-news exhaustion
guides.concept: A catalyst is an issuer or market event hypothesized to affect attention and price; the correct decision requires a verified public-time chronology and observed price response.
guides.watchFor: Check primary filing or issuer notice, effective timestamp and timezone, symbol identity, first tradable session, volume and key structure before labeling a catalyst strong.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative continuation entry needs independently observable market confirmation after the public event and acceptable costs, not a social post stating the stock will rise.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires the event interpretation and chart structure to remain compatible with the plan; later contradictory disclosures or structural failures require fresh analysis.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows changed material disclosures, confirmed failed response, planned target or time exit, or unacceptable volatility/halts.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if the catalyst source is unverified or publication time falls after the replay pause. NO TRADE when identity, share count, spreads or data rights are uncertain.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A press release timestamped 16:05 cannot be used to justify a strategy decision recorded at 15:40 that same day.
guides.procedure: At a declared replay pause point, first check the setup and source constraints. Check primary filing or issuer notice, effective timestamp and timezone, symbol identity, first tradable session, volume and key structure before labeling a catalyst strong.

guides.title: Position hold partial exit trailing stop and time exit
guides.concept: A position-management plan distinguishes an intact trade thesis from the independent reasons to reduce or close exposure, and requires order-state awareness.
guides.watchFor: Before entry record the planned horizon, invalidation, size, first objective, partial-exit rule, trailing criteria, maximum duration, cost assumptions and alternate no-trade choice.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative entry remains a hypothetical scenario if fills are not verified; the model needs price-distance and available-liquidity checks before any quantity is contemplated.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is justified only while the original premise and risk controls remain valid; an unrealized gain, loss aversion or desire to recover are not evidence.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit or partial-exit review follows predetermined targets, structural failure, time limit, unplanned spread changes or a risk limit; verify actual filled versus remaining shares.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when a new signal lacks confirmation; NO TRADE or seek a correction when order cancellation/partial-fill status is uncertain and actual exposure cannot be measured.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: An order for 200 shares filled 75, and its cancel request remains pending. A chart-based hold/exit discussion must not pretend all 200 shares were acquired.
guides.procedure: At a declared replay pause point, first check the setup and source constraints. Before entry record the planned horizon, invalidation, size, first objective, partial-exit rule, trailing criteria, maximum duration, cost assumptions and alternate no-trade choice.
